record.original_question: Develop a similar theory of limit shapes for Young–Fibonacci diagrams. The initial challenge is defining a concept of scaling between smaller and larger diagrams. E.g., if the scaling is a doubling, we need to define an embeddingDofYF_r intoYF_r that maps words (diagrams) of sizekinto words of size 2k,YF (k) r →YF (2k) r . The embedding should be “nearly isometric” in that it maps words that are “near” each other inYF_r (in the distance metric of the Hasse diagram) into words that are near each otherYF_r, and vice-versa. And every word inYF_r must be near an element of the image ofD. Given such a doubling map, it defines a limit space within which the question can be asked whether randomlychosenr-colored permutations have a limit shape. If there is a limit shape, determine it. SinceYF_r as dual graded graphs has a unique weighting 1, there are no colorings of the tableaux, so there are only three distributions of diagrams to be considered.

And every word inYF r must be near an element of the image ofD. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The Young–Fibonacci lattice YF is the graded poset whose elements at rank k are the words on the alphabet {1,2} whose digits sum to k (Fibonacci words of size k). The covering relations are: a word w covers w' if w' is obtained from w either by deleting the leftmost 1 of w, or by replacing the leftmost 2 (occurring before any 1) of w by 1 (equivalently, reading covers from below: from a word v one builds a covering w by either prepending a 1 to v, or by changing the first 1 of v into a 2). The Hasse diagram of YF endows the set of Fibonacci words with a graph distance d. For an integer r ≥ 1, let YF_r denote the r-differential analogue of the Young–Fibonacci lattice (the dual graded graph obtained from the unique weighting equal to 1 on YF, augmented with r colors when applicable; in the case of YF_r as dual graded graphs there is a unique weighting and no nontrivial coloring of tableaux). For each k let YF^{(k)}_r be the set of words of size k.

Problem. 
(a) Define a notion of scaling (a "doubling map") for YF_r: construct, for every k, an embedding D : YF^{(k)}_r → YF^{(2k)}_r such that
  (i) D is nearly isometric: there exist constants C, C' (independent of k) such that for all words u, v ∈ YF^{(k)}_r,
        |d(D(u), D(v)) − 2·d(u, v)| ≤ C,
   and conversely any pair of words near each other in the image corresponds to a pair of words near each other in YF^{(k)}_r;
  (ii) D is nearly surjective: every word w ∈ YF^{(2k)}_r lies within distance ≤ C' of D(YF^{(k)}_r).

(b) Using such a doubling map, form the corresponding inverse/direct limit metric space (the "limit space"). Considering each of the three natural probability distributions on Young–Fibonacci diagrams of size n (the Plancherel-type measure coming from r-colored permutations and the other two distributions naturally associated to YF_r as dual graded graphs), determine whether a uniformly random r-colored permutation of size n yields, after appropriate rescaling via D, a limit shape inside this limit space. If a limit shape exists, identify it explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this problem was located. It is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on the combinatorics of tableaux, and there is no evidence in the literature that a theory of limit shapes for Young–Fibonacci diagrams (analogous to the Vershik–Kerov–Logan–Shepp theory for Young diagrams) has been established.
